As we wrap up our journey through Mistakes Were Made (But Not by Me), let’s take a moment to bring it all together.
This isn’t about chasing down every error, or living with self-doubt. It’s really about noticing those quiet ways our minds try to protect us—catching ourselves before we double down, and choosing honesty, even when it stings a little.
What stands out from all of this? Self-justification is something we all do—our brains are wired for it. Our memories and beliefs are shaped much more by our need to feel right than by cold, hard facts. But here’s what’s powerful: honest reflection and a real apology can break those cycles of denial, and actually heal relationships.
Whether you’re seeking justice, healing, or just more peace in your day-to-day, it all comes down to putting truth above pride—and having the humility to ask yourself tough questions. That’s where growth really begins.
So, if you catch yourself defending a mistake, take a breath. You’re not alone—we all do it. But every moment gives you a choice: you can hold onto the comfort of being right, or you can lean into the discomfort—and the freedom—of being honest.
This path isn’t always easy, but it’s the one that leads to deeper connections, wiser decisions, and a life that feels true to who you are. Mistakes? They’re just part of being human. What matters most is what you do next.
Choose clarity. Choose courage. And remember—the real strength isn’t about never being wrong. It’s about being willing to see, to learn, and to grow.
